minutes.headline: Board leaned to the smaller TC Passios office option but kept it on the agenda; police mutual aid vote held for training info.
minutes.summary: The board ratified two police hires and an interim building commissioner, heard the architect's cost options for consolidating town offices at TC Passios, and reviewed a draft noise bylaw and special event permit policy. what_happened.line: The board heard the architect's cost options for consolidating town offices at TC Passios and reached no resolution, keeping it as a regular agenda item.
The board held the Middlesex police mutual aid agreement, tabling it pending training information.
The board ratified the town manager's appointment of two full-time police officers.
The board changed the closing date of the special Town Meeting warrant to October 11, 2018 at 5 p.m.
The board reviewed a draft noise bylaw and special event permit policy, and a draft article would transfer from a salary reserve to fund the first year of the DPW contract.

why_it_matters: The TC Passios option the board chooses sets how much the town budget, mostly taxes, may be asked to spend on office space, and Town Meeting voters could be asked to approve it.

The noise bylaw and event permit policy would set rules for residents and event hosts, and the DPW contract's first-year funding is a transfer that the special Town Meeting warrant may ask voters to approve.
watch_next: The special Town Meeting warrant closes October 11, 2018 at 5 p.m.
A workshop with the School Committee was proposed for November 7th.
